figures.caption: The initial publication contains one pending cell and no selected route.
figures.alt: Five annotated details at the initial maze ready boundary. Only cell zero at column zero row zero is frontier. Cells one, eight and nine are unseen and the other sixty cells are walls. Parent bytes are all 255; only the start distance is zero. Head is zero, tail one, current minus one, phase zero, result minus one and length minus one.

figures.caption: Expanding the start discovers two neighbors at distance one.
figures.alt: Five annotated details after processing start cell zero. Its state is two, meaning processed. Cells one and eight are frontier with state one; cell nine is unseen. Both newly discovered parents are zero and both distances are one. Head is one, tail three, current zero, phase one. Result and route length remain minus one.

figures.caption: The final small-room publication selects a two-edge shortest route.
figures.alt: Five annotated details at final phase two. All four open cells are processed with state two. Parents connect nine to one to zero and distance nine is two. Route cells are zero, one and nine, colored blue; processed cell eight stays green. Head and tail are four, current nine, result one and route length two.

figures.caption: All queue slots retain discovery history while the final active frontier is empty.
figures.alt: Four annotated details for an open eight by eight room with goal sixty-three. Queue storage contains sixty-four distinct cell IDs, including goal sixty-three in the last slot. The route follows all eight top-row cells and then the seven remaining right-column cells, giving fifteen cells and fourteen edges. Head and tail are sixty-four, phase two, result one and length fourteen.
